title: Her Hair Fell Out. She Built an Empire.

brand.cta: Follow The Black History Room for one story a day.

beats.text: Her hair fell out. She built an empire.

overlays.hook: Her hair fell out. *She built an empire.*

beats.text: Born Sarah Breedlove in 1867, on a Louisiana plantation, the first in her family born free.
Orphaned at seven. Married at fourteen. A widow at twenty.
In St. Louis, she washed clothes for a dollar fifty a day.
In the 1890s, a scalp disease took most of her hair. She went looking for a cure.

visual.caption: Madam C. J. Walker, by Addison Scurlock, c. 1912

beats.text: In 1905, she moved to Denver and sold her own hair grower door to door.

visual.title: Door to door
visual.caption: Madam C. J. Walker Preparations, advertisement, 1920

beats.text: By 1910, she had a factory and beauty school in Indianapolis.

visual.caption: The Madam C. J. Walker Mfg. Co., Indianapolis, 1911

beats.text: Thousands of Black women became Walker agents. One had earned five dollars a week as a maid. Now, 250.
In 1919, she gave five thousand dollars to the NAACP to fight lynching, its largest gift ever.
She built a mansion on the Hudson, by a Black architect.
She died there in 1919, at 51, worth over a million dollars. The washerwoman became one of America's richest Black women.

facts.claim: Born Sarah Breedlove, 23 Dec 1867, on a plantation in Delta, Louisiana; first child in the family born after Emancipation.
Orphaned at seven; married Moses McWilliams at 14; widowed around 1887 (daughter Lelia born 1885).
Washerwoman in St. Louis for as little as $1.50 a day.
1890s scalp ailment made most of her hair fall out.
Moved to Denver in 1905 (first as Annie Malone's agent), then sold her own hair grower.
Headquarters in Indianapolis by 1910, with a factory and a beauty school.
Several thousand agents; at the Aug 1917 convention Margaret Thompson said she had earned $5 a week as a servant and now $250 a week.
May 1919 pledge of $5,000 to the NAACP anti-lynching fund; NAACP secretary Shillady called it the largest gift the Association had ever received.
Villa Lewaro, Irvington-on-Hudson, built 1918, designed by African American architect Vertner Tandy.
Died 25 May 1919 at Villa Lewaro, aged 51; total assets well over $1,000,000; one of the wealthiest Black women of her time.

notUsed: 'First self-made female millionaire' (Guinness): she denied being a millionaire in her lifetime (Indiana Historical Society) and others may have come before her; the reel says 'assets of more than a million dollars' and 'one of the richest'
Her savings on arriving in Denver ($1.25 / $1.50, varies by source)
Agent totals (several thousand / 23,000 / 40,000, varies by source)
The $250 a week is Thompson's own claim at the convention
